innovation_lens: Auxiliary lens calibrated to early NVIDIA, Tesla, Palantir, Google and Amazon. It tests category creation, structural-wave exposure, founder/reinvestment behavior, product velocity, customer pull/expansion, platform optionality and power-law potential. It does not modify the 100-point policy weights or override Hard Veto.
core_thesis: Rubrik has moved beyond legacy backup into cyber resilience and is attempting a second category expansion into identity and agentic-AI control. The strongest evidence is the existing engine: Subscription ARR $1.66B growing 33%, Cloud ARR $1.48B growing 39%, >119% dollar-based net retention, 3,084 customers above $100K ARR, ~80% TTM gross margin and rapidly improving contribution/operating leverage. Rubrik Agent Cloud can create a second growth curve because Rubrik already owns immutable historical state, application context, identity context and recovery workflows; however RAC economic contribution is not separately disclosed.
current_finding: TTM revenue is about $1.542B, TTM company-defined FCF about $286M (18.6% margin), GAAP operating margin about -18.3%, and TTM SBC about $342M or 22.2% of revenue. A mechanical FCF-minus-SBC diagnostic is slightly negative. FY27 guidance implies ~28% revenue and ARR growth and ~38% FCF growth. Business economics are improving faster than GAAP earnings, but shareholder economics are not mature.
capital_and_survival: At July 31, 2026 Rubrik held about $1.75B of cash and short-term investments versus $1.15B principal of 0% convertible notes due 2030. Operations generate positive cash and external capital is not needed for survival. The principal capital-allocation risk is equity compensation and future reinvestment/M&A discipline, not balance-sheet fragility.
permanent_loss_case: Rubrik remains relevant but fails to become a durable control plane. Backup/data protection gets bundled, RAC remains a feature rather than a platform, NRR and new ARR slow, sales efficiency stalls, and SBC stays above ~15-20% of revenue. The company survives but per-share owner cash disappoints while a premium forward ARR multiple compresses.

evidence: Cyber resilience is becoming a core security category as ransomware, identity attacks and autonomous agents increase the cost of bad state changes.
Rubrik expanded from backup/recovery into RSC, identity resilience and RAC; 2026 Gartner recognition indicates sustained category leadership in backup/data protection.
RAC, Agent Rewind and Rubrik AI attempt to define a runtime-control/recovery layer for autonomous agents.
counter_evidence: RAC is commercially new and its financial contribution is unknown.
Incumbents and hyperscalers have greater distribution and can bundle adjacent security/control capabilities.
missing_data: RAC ARR, attach rate, customer count and renewal/expansion cohorts.

evidence: Subscription ARR +33%, Cloud ARR +39%, >119% DBNRR and $100K+ ARR customers +23% show strong expansion and large-enterprise pull.
Recovery, identity rollback and immutable state restoration solve high-cost mission-critical problems.
Microsoft Defender integration and Claude Code/Project Hourglass broaden workflow fit and distribution.
counter_evidence: No independent cohort-level ROI or gross retention disclosure; channel structure obscures some end-customer economics.
missing_data: Gross retention, RAC-specific NRR, sales-cycle and competitive win/loss data.

evidence: Rubrik's time-series/self-describing data architecture combines application, identity, sensitivity and lineage context with immutable recovery state.
The platform becomes more valuable as customers protect more workloads and identities; switching a recovery system carries operational/compliance friction.
Seven consecutive years of Gartner Leader positioning and expanding integrations suggest widening enterprise credibility and ecosystem reach.
counter_evidence: There is no strong network effect comparable with Google, and data advantages are customer-specific rather than globally compounding.
Large vendors can integrate backup, identity, cloud and security products; open cloud/AI stacks may reduce differentiation.
missing_data: Independent market-share trend, win/loss cohorts, pricing power and renewal by product bundle.

evidence: Subscription ARR contribution margin improved to 14.0% from 9.4%, while S&M and G&A ratios show operating leverage.
FY26 OCF rose to $282.9M and FCF to $237.8M; FY27 FCF guidance midpoint $328M implies ~38% growth.
High gross margin and SaaS transition create a plausible path to strong incremental margins.
counter_evidence: TTM SBC is ~22% of revenue and exceeds company-defined TTM FCF; economic owner cash is not yet proven.
Period-end share count rose about 2.5% from Jan 31 to Aug 24, 2026 and unrecognized RSU compensation remains large.
R&D/AI spend is accelerating and realized incremental return is not yet measurable.
missing_data: Normalized SBC path, per-share owner FCF and RAC cohort return on R&D/sales spend.

evidence: Founder-CEO Bipul Sinha retains substantial economic/voting exposure and management continues aggressive R&D through a structural transition rather than harvesting near-term margins.
The company completed an appliance/term-license to SaaS transition while sustaining >30% ARR growth and moving to positive FCF.
0% convertible financing with capped calls reduced near-term financing cost and partly mitigates conversion dilution.
counter_evidence: Dual-class control gives insiders/affiliates about 78% voting power, reducing outside-shareholder influence.
SBC remains very high and is the largest open capital-allocation question.
missing_data: Long-run SBC target/discipline and acquisition-return history at larger scale.

evidence: ~$1.75B cash and short-term investments exceed the $1.15B convertible principal; positive OCF/FCF reduce financing risk.
Convertible notes carry 0% coupon and mature in 2030; capped calls reduce dilution within their contractual range.
~80% TTM gross margin provides substantial gross-profit cushion.
counter_evidence: A large majority of protected on-prem data still relies on Rubrik-branded appliances built on Supermicro servers.
The convertible note becomes a dilution/cash-settlement consideration if share price rises above conversion economics.

evidence: At $86.65 and ~207.3M shares, equity value is ~$18.0B and EV ~$17.35B; FY27 midpoint implies ~10.3x EV/revenue and ~9.2x EV/ARR.
A 10-year owner-cash DCF that explicitly charges SBC implies the current price needs about 18.9% annual revenue growth for a decade plus ~25% mature owner-cash margin.
Bull value can exceed current price materially if RAC creates a second growth curve and SBC normalizes.
counter_evidence: Base scenario around $72/share is below the reference price; probability-weighted scenario value is around the high-$70s under conservative owner-cash assumptions.
Forward company-defined FCF yield is only ~1.8%, and company FCF excludes SBC as a cash outflow.
missing_data: Verified post-Sep-11 price and evidence of sustainable SBC reduction/RAC monetization.

evidence: If Rubrik becomes the resilience/control plane for enterprise data, identity and agents, its addressable value can grow far beyond backup and a $30B+ equity outcome is plausible.
The business is capital-light, mission-critical and already scaled enough that new product success can distribute through an existing enterprise base.
counter_evidence: Current ~$18B equity value already prices substantial success; unlike early Amazon/Google/NVIDIA, Rubrik is not starting from a tiny valuation relative to an obviously massive winner-take-most market.
Bear-case downside is severe if growth normalizes and SBC remains high; asymmetric upside is good but not yet extraordinary at the reference price.
missing_data: RAC economics and independent evidence that Rubrik can own a cross-vendor agent-control standard.

innovation_archetype_comparison.overall: Rubrik shows a meaningful early-innovator pattern, strongest in the Palantir and infrastructure-control-point aspects of early NVIDIA. It is less similar to early Google because it lacks a global network-effect flywheel, and less similar to early Amazon because its current valuation already assumes significant category success.

NVIDIA.reason: Like early NVIDIA, Rubrik is trying to turn a technical architecture into a standard control layer for a new computing regime. Missing proof is ecosystem/developer lock-in and design-standard dominance comparable with GPU platform adoption.

Tesla.reason: Founder-led category redefinition against entrenched incumbents and investment ahead of current profit resemble Tesla. Rubrik is far less capital intensive and lacks a comparable physical-product bottleneck.

Palantir.reason: Mission-critical enterprise software, strong founder control, sticky deployments, expanding platform scope, high SBC, and customer value that can compound as more critical workflows/data move onto the platform are strongly analogous.

Google.reason: High gross margin and product engineering fit, but Rubrik lacks Google's two-sided advertiser/user network effect and was not GAAP-profitable at a comparable early-public stage.

Amazon.reason: Land-and-expand, customer trust, reinvestment and adjacency expansion from backup to cyber resilience/identity/AI control resemble Amazon's early platform-expansion logic; the gap is slower market-scale expansion and a higher starting valuation relative to revenue.

items.evidence: KPMG opined FY2026 financial statements were fairly presented and ICFR was effective; Q2 FY2027 disclosure controls remained effective.
Positive OCF/FCF and ~$1.75B liquid assets versus $1.15B convertible principal; operations do not require fresh capital to survive.

TTM SBC is ~22% of revenue; period-end shares rose ~2.5% in under seven months and unrecognized RSU expense remains large. High growth currently offsets dilution but long-duration shareholder dilution is not yet controlled.
items.resolution_needed: Require SBC/revenue to trend toward low-teens then <10%, and per-share owner FCF to compound despite vesting.

items.evidence: ARR, Cloud ARR, large-customer count, DBNRR and normalized revenue all grow strongly; expansion is not dependent on acquisitions or subsidies.
items.resolution_needed: Monitor sales efficiency as material-right transition fades.

items.evidence: Contribution margin, FCF and opex ratios are improving while R&D investment rises; no evidence of structural return collapse.
items.resolution_needed: Prove RAC/AI R&D converts into ARR and owner cash.

items.evidence: Product breadth and integrations are expanding while ARR/cloud ARR and large-customer counts grow >20%; current evidence indicates widening rather than shrinking moat.
items.resolution_needed: Track competitive win/loss and identity/AI attach rates.

items.evidence: Reference price requires roughly 19% decade revenue CAGR and 25% mature owner-cash margin. Demanding, but not necessarily unrealistic for a durable category leader currently growing ARR >30%.
items.resolution_needed: Reopen if clean ARR growth falls below ~20% before owner margin/SBC improves.

items.evidence: Top three channel partners and affiliates generated ~68% of FY2026 revenue, and a large majority of appliance-based protected data depends on Supermicro hardware. This is distribution/supply concentration rather than one end-customer dependency, but it is material.
items.resolution_needed: Need evidence of channel diversification/direct-cloud distribution and reduced appliance/Supermicro dependency without slower growth.

items.evidence: Solvency risk is low. Permanent loss would more likely come from competitive commoditization, failed RAC monetization, persistent dilution and valuation compression.
items.resolution_needed: Monitor moat and per-share owner-cash falsifiers.

attacks: RAC may be narrative extension: security vendors, hyperscalers and agent platforms can build native governance/rollback before Rubrik establishes a standard.
Backup/cyber-recovery leadership may not transfer into runtime agent security; product adjacency is not automatically moat adjacency.
DBNRR >119% is good but declining at the margin, and transition benefits/material rights complicate headline growth comparability.
Company-defined FCF looks strong because SBC is non-cash; TTM SBC exceeds TTM FCF, so owner economics can be materially weaker.
Top-three channel partners generate ~68% of revenue; partner reprioritization can disrupt go-to-market despite end-customer diversity.
Supermicro remains a concentrated appliance dependency for much of protected enterprise data.
Dual-class governance gives insiders/affiliates decisive control, reducing external discipline.
The market already understands the cyber-resilience/AI-control story at ~9x forward ARR; narrative success can coexist with mediocre stock returns.
Large incumbents can bundle backup, identity and AI security with broader endpoint/cloud/security suites.
A slowdown in ransomware/AI-security budgets or enterprise IT optimization could expose a long sales cycle and large S&M base.
red_team.strongest_bear_thesis: Rubrik is an excellent, sticky backup/cyber-recovery company whose AI-control story never becomes a separate economic platform. Growth falls toward the mid-teens, channel and bundle competition cap pricing, SBC remains high, and the stock derates from a premium ARR multiple. The company remains healthy while shareholders earn poor returns.
hidden_assumptions: RSC data/identity context genuinely transfers into a durable RAC control-plane advantage.
SBC/revenue falls much faster than growth without damaging talent/product velocity.
Current >30% ARR growth remains >20% long enough to justify a premium terminal franchise.
red_team.independence: Same analyst/model; not an independent second-party red team.

falsifiers: Subscription ARR growth falls below 20% for two consecutive quarters while DBNRR is <=110%.
Cloud ARR growth falls below Subscription ARR growth for two consecutive quarters after migration effects normalize.
RAC has no disclosed material ARR/customer adoption or attach-rate evidence by FY2028 despite continued heavy AI R&D.
SBC remains >18% of revenue through FY2028 and shares grow >5% annually while owner cash per share stagnates.
Subscription ARR contribution margin stops improving or falls below 12% without a deliberate high-return investment explanation.
Top-three channel partner share remains near or above 70% and a major partner materially reduces Rubrik prioritization.
A major security/cloud platform wins credible integrated recovery + identity + agent rollback and Rubrik's win rates/NRR deteriorate.
Gross margin remains below ~78% while revenue growth slows below 20%, eliminating the operating-leverage thesis.
increase_evidence: Two or more quarters of >25% clean Subscription ARR growth and >30% Cloud ARR growth after transition/material-right effects become immaterial.
RAC reports material customer/ARR contribution, strong attach into existing RSC accounts and evidence of cross-vendor agent governance.
SBC/revenue trends below ~15% with owner FCF/share turning clearly positive and compounding >20%.
Subscription ARR contribution margin reaches high-teens/20%+ while R&D remains productive.
Channel concentration and Supermicro dependency decline without slower growth.
Price falls enough to provide >25% upside to a conservative base case without deterioration in business evidence.
sell_reduce_evidence: ARR growth and DBNRR break the falsifier thresholds.
RAC is displaced by native hyperscaler/model-provider agent governance before material monetization.
SBC dilution remains structurally high and per-share owner economics fail to improve.
A major accounting/security trust failure occurs in Rubrik's own control plane.
Channel/supply concentration causes repeated execution failures.
Valuation remains premium while moat/growth evidence weakens together.
portfolio_context: No holding size, tax basis, target allocation or current portfolio risk budget was provided in this run. The harness therefore assigns WATCH and no buy authorization/position size.
